# MM-P3-L1-IH03 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

## Scope
This document covers maintenance tasks required to verify operation and safety of Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03). Tasks include inspection of electrical connections, coil cooling water system verification, control system health check, and confirmation of billet heating performance. Reference applicable safety bulletins and operating procedures: SB-1044, SB-1047, SOP-P3-L1-05.

## Tools
- Insulated hand tools suitable for industrial electrical work  
- Portable thermal sensor or pyrometer capable of reading target billet temperature  
- Flow meter compatible with coil cooling water circuit  
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P3-L1-05

## Procedure
- Isolate equipment per SOP-P3-L1-05 and verify lockout/tagout compliance before any maintenance access.  
- Inspect coil assembly for signs of damage, wear, or loose fittings. Confirm electrical connections are clean and secure.  
- Restore power and perform control system diagnostics guided by SB-1044 and SB-1047. Verify alarms and interlocks function per manufacturer guidance.  
- Measure coil cooling water flow using the flow meter at the coil inlet and outlet locations. Confirm measured flow meets or exceeds the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03): 65 L/min.  
- Run a heating cycle with a test billet following SOP-P3-L1-05. Monitor billet temperature using the portable thermal sensor or pyrometer. Confirm heating profile achieves the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03): 1260 °C.  
- If any parameter fails to meet acceptance criteria, tag component out of service and escalate per SB-1044.

## Acceptance criteria
- Coil cooling water flow equals or exceeds 65 L/min.  
- Billet reaches 1260 °C under normal operating control conditions as defined in SOP-P3-L1-05.  
- No active electrical faults or unaddressed mechanical defects remain.  
- All tests and corrective actions documented and filed per plant document control.
